note: Disable Login Page adds a route access check to user.login / user.login.http that forbids the login page unless the request carries ?<querystring>=<secret>. Config object disable_login.settings has three keys: disable_login (bool master switch), querystring (parameter name), secret (required value). Configure route disable_login.settings_form (/admin/config/security/disable-login), core 'administer site configuration' permission. No config/install ships, so protection is off until configured. Secret can be altered via hook_disable_login_key_alter(&$secret). Cases are grounded in these keys; medium/hard scripts set and read them and always disable protection on cleanup/reset so login is never left locked.

evals.prompt: With the disable_login module protecting my Drupal login page using querystring name 'key' and secret value 'abc123', what URL lets an authorised user reach the login form, and what happens without it?
evals.expected_output: Visit /user/login?key=abc123 to reach the form; /user/login without the correct querystring/value returns Access Denied (403).

evals.prompt: Which configuration values does the disable_login module use to protect the login page, and where is the settings page?
evals.expected_output: Config object disable_login.settings with keys disable_login (on/off), querystring (parameter name) and secret (required value). Settings at Configuration > Security > Disable Login Page (/admin/config/security/disable-login).

evals.prompt: How can a developer make the disable_login secret key change automatically (for example rotate it monthly) instead of hard-coding one value?
evals.expected_output: Implement hook_disable_login_key_alter(&$secret) in a custom module and assign the computed value to $secret (it is passed by reference); the access check uses the altered value.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has the login page protected by the disable_login module. Inspect the live configuration and give the exact URL an authorised user must use to reach /user/login.
evals.expected_output: disable_login.settings has disable_login=true, querystring=entry, secret=sesame, so the URL is /user/login?entry=sesame.

evals.prompt: Is anonymous access to the /user/login page currently restricted by the disable_login module on this site? Inspect the live configuration to answer yes/no and explain.
evals.expected_output: Yes: disable_login.settings -> disable_login is true, so the access check forbids /user/login unless the request has ?entry=sesame.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the disable_login module to block anonymous access to /user/login unless the request includes the querystring parameter 'gate' with the value 'openup'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set disable_login.settings: disable_login=true, querystring='gate', secret='openup' (e.g. drush cset disable_login.settings disable_login 1; ... querystring gate; ... secret openup). Then /user/login?gate=openup reaches the form.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site already protects /user/login with the disable_login module. Rotate the credentials so the login page now requires the querystring parameter 'pass' with the value 'letmein' (keeping protection enabled). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Keep disable_login.settings:disable_login=true and set querystring='pass', secret='letmein', so the working URL becomes /user/login?pass=letmein.
